resources.string: Import an installed game folder. Your files stay where they are.
This downloads and installs the GLIBC runtime (Wine, X11, graphics drivers) needed to launch GLIBC games. It can take a few minutes.
This builds the shared RootFS base runtime (box64, Wine, and fonts) that new game containers are cloned from. It can take a few minutes.
This deletes the current shared RootFS base and rebuilds it from scratch. Already-installed games keep working; this can take a few minutes.
The templates are ready-made Wine prefixes that new games clone. They can be rebuilt, so leaving them out makes the backup smaller; a restore then rebuilds them, which takes a few extra minutes.
Build the base environment before backing it up.
This replaces the current shared RootFS base and Wine prefix templates with your saved backup. Already-installed games keep working; this can take a few minutes.

Manage KWin desktop distributions that run natively in Termux or inside a proot container. Install once, then open one to start it on the built-in display.
A native desktop runs its compositor directly in Termux on Android system GLES.
Container desktops run the session inside a proot distro. The same combination can be created more than once.
Created environments are hidden: native mode allows one instance per environment.
Container mode keeps every created desktop in the option list: each creation gets its own container instance. The rootfs tarball is downloaded once and cached; later instances install from cache.
Lightweight DE, XRender compositing on the host GPU
